proposals.instruction: Score 10 when domain structure, symmetry, constraints, or relational geometry is mapped to a specific architectural or objective choice and the preserved information is explained; score 0 when a fashionable mechanism is used without structural justification.
proposals.rationale: R18 uses rotational symmetry, R43 uses spectral graph structure, and R52 uses higher-order relational structure to motivate their designs.

proposals.name: Principled Simplification
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the work removes a conventional component or assumption through a stated argument about what function is actually necessary; score 0 when it only adds modules, losses, or machinery.
proposals.rationale: R19 fixes the classifier rather than learning it, R22 minimizes task-specific machinery, and R29 removes perceptual supervision through a redesigned discriminator.

proposals.name: Cross-Regime Generalization Design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the method is deliberately constructed and evaluated across materially different domains, tasks, or distribution regimes that probe transfer; score 0 when it is confined to one narrowly matched setting.
proposals.rationale: R20 studies synthetic distribution mismatch, R31 covers text- and image-guided translation, and R48 contrasts original with counterfactually altered data.

proposals.name: Scarcity Leverage
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the method explicitly exploits sparse data, limited interaction, scarce viewpoints, or tight computation through a reusable structural advantage; score 0 when it assumes abundant resources or merely reports generic efficiency.
proposals.rationale: R01 leverages extremely limited gameplay, R42 transfers multi-view priors from scarce viewpoints, and R17 addresses ultra-high-resolution inputs under constrained computation.

proposals.name: Nuisance and Degeneracy Control
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract anticipates a concrete nuisance or degenerate solution and includes a principled safeguard tied to that failure; score 0 when such failure modes are ignored.
proposals.rationale: R17 prevents sampling trivial backgrounds, R47 controls outliers and unrealistic deformations, and R37 exposes experimental artifacts that otherwise drive predictions.

proposals.name: Ambiguity Awareness
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the work recognizes multiple valid explanations, solutions, or latent rewards and designs its objective or inference procedure accordingly; score 0 when it assumes an unjustified unique target.
proposals.rationale: R41 explicitly handles multiple valid combinatorial solutions, R04 addresses validity among many discrete sequences, and R50 confronts underdetermined rewards from demonstrations.

proposals.name: Operational Specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract specifies the essential mechanism, assumptions, data conditions, and evaluation setup well enough to reconstruct the contribution; score 0 when it consists mainly of slogans or unnamed architectural additions.
proposals.rationale: R58 provides almost no operational content, while R32 and R54 describe broad architectural additions with limited detail about their concrete mechanisms.

proposals.name: Discriminating Evaluation Design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the evaluation includes comparisons, controls, ablations, or varied conditions that distinguish the proposed explanation from plausible alternatives; score 0 when it relies mainly on generic benchmark claims.
proposals.rationale: R30 emphasizes many tasks and baselines without clearly isolating the ranking hypothesis, while R54 and R29 emphasize broad improvements with limited evidence separating individual design choices.

proposals.name: Scope and Assumption Honesty
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract clearly states operating regimes, limitations, and the boundary between proved claims and empirical observations; score 0 when narrow evidence is presented as broadly universal.
proposals.rationale: R56 explicitly distinguishes progressive-reward settings from standard games, whereas R10 and R59 make broad superiority or generality claims with less clearly stated boundaries.

proposals.name: Reusable Conceptual Unification
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the work introduces an abstraction that connects previously separate methods or settings and yields concrete reusable deductions; score 0 when it is mainly a renamed combination of existing components.
proposals.rationale: R53 unifies several Lipschitz-layer constructions algebraically, R13 develops a transferable symbolic view of learned optimizers, and R55 reframes contrastive learning through augmentation overlap.

proposals.name: Abstract verbosity
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much unusually extended exposition, qualification, and contextual detail the abstract contains; judge only extent, not whether the detail is good or bad.
proposals.rationale: R04 and R05 provide unusually long, multi-part descriptions with extensive setup and evaluation detail, whereas R02 and R33 are extremely brief.

proposals.name: Acronym and method-name density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract introduces named methods, abbreviations, and component labels; judge only extent, not whether the naming is useful or technically good.
proposals.rationale: R12 introduces PAPO and several named components, and R24 introduces HYSP alongside multiple specialized terms; R02 and R07 likewise foreground distinctive named methods.

proposals.name: Numerical result density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract contains explicit percentages, scores, timing figures, complexity bounds, or other numerical results; judge only extent, not the magnitude or desirability of the results.
proposals.rationale: R14 contains several compression and accuracy percentages, while R37 prominently reports batch size and training time; R51 also contains multiple exact verification figures.

proposals.name: Reproducibility signaling
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract explicitly mentions released code, models, datasets, or reproduction resources; judge only extent, not whether the resources are genuinely useful.
proposals.rationale: R15, R16, R21, R24, R37, and R54 explicitly advertise code or models, making resource-release language a visible stylistic channel independent of scientific quality.

proposals.name: Formal-theory signaling
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract uses theorem, proof, bound, convergence, asymptotic, or formal mathematical-guarantee language; judge only extent, not correctness or importance.
proposals.rationale: R04, R08, R29, R40, and R55 prominently use formal guarantees and asymptotic claims. Authorial training or seniority may produce this fingerprint and may also correlate with genuine technical quality, so it is mixed.

proposals.name: Benchmark breadth signaling
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract lists many datasets, tasks, domains, baselines, or application settings; judge only extent, not whether the coverage is convincing.
proposals.rationale: R05 cites 12 baselines, 16 search spaces, and 86 tasks, while R36 spans up to 44 languages and several corpora. Resources and collaborations can create this fingerprint and can also support better research, so it is mixed.

proposals.name: Editorial polish
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of fluent grammar, consistent terminology, smooth transitions, and carefully standardized prose; judge only textual polish, not research quality.
proposals.rationale: R47 and R54 use highly smooth, carefully staged exposition, while R31 and R49 contain visible grammatical awkwardness and less standardized phrasing. Professional editing can affect reception without itself being research quality.

proposals.name: Trend anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract frames the work through phrases such as recent success, emerging interest, current limitations, or rapidly developing research directions; judge only extent, not topical importance.
proposals.rationale: R21, R26, R30, and R41 repeatedly anchor their motivation in recent or emerging developments. Submission timing and topical fashion can leave this textual trace without constituting research quality.

proposals.name: Community-specific jargon
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract relies on dense subfield vocabulary, specialized acronyms, and assumed community knowledge without defining every term; judge only extent, not whether the terminology is appropriate.
proposals.rationale: R26 and R32 use concentrated graph-learning and spectral terminology, while R35 and R50 use specialized Bayesian-process language. Community membership produces this fingerprint and may also reflect genuine expertise, so it is mixed.

proposals.name: Resource-scale signaling
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract mentions unusually large hardware, datasets, real-world systems, language coverage, or computational scale; judge only extent, not whether the scale improves the work.
proposals.rationale: R37 highlights TPU-scale training and massive batches, R36 reports multilingual coverage up to 44 languages, and R19 mentions real robotic systems and simulations. Institutional resources create this visible signal and may also enable genuinely stronger experiments, so it is mixed.
